x-protocol-rules.identityBinding: Agent Commons assigns a permanent, nonrecycled production partnerId to each public enrollment. Independently prove the exact primary website host and exact handoff authority, including a different subdomain. A host can have one current production primary identity. Retain historical binding and audit evidence on death, transfer or domain loss. An expired binding cannot be claimed as the prior identity. Never authorize work using names, a public badge, group membership or referrer alone.
x-protocol-rules.domainProof: Issue a random 256-bit TXT challenge under _agentcommons.<exact canonical host>, valid for 24 hours and bound to the application, revision, purpose, environment and candidate host. Verify the site's own authoritative DNS observations, respecting DNSSEC where deployed. Reject signed-zone validation failures and local/private names. Use a uniqueness transaction at successful activation; an outstanding unproved claim never locks the domain. DNS TXT is public; sight of the nonce alone is not evidence. Recheck presence at least daily; proofs require a fresh nonce at least every 30 days. A scoped renewal agent can rotate the TXT at day 20. Retain the last material identity revision during successful same-domain renewal. Do not extend deadlines on DNS errors. validUntil is the earlier of last successful observation plus 24 hours and fresh challenge validation plus 30 days. Confirmed loss, conflict, suspension or revocation takes effect immediately. On proof expiry block new selection, grants, commands and active badges, and preserve existing obligations for recovery. A replacement requires fresh proof before switching, freezes old grants for new effects and increments the identity revision. Historical receipts retain the old binding.
x-protocol-rules.nameComparison: Pin Unicode 17.0.0 data and compare normalized public names and full IDN hosts. Preserve validated display text; reject unsafe direction overrides and controls. The comparison key uses NFKC_Casefold, then removes Unicode White_Space and Punctuation. The strongest name reason wins in order: original scalar equality, normalized equality, UTS #39 skeleton equality of normalized keys, then restricted Damerau-Levenshtein distance (optimal string alignment on scalar values). Near match threshold is one when the shorter normalized key contains at least five scalars, two when it contains at least twelve, and zero otherwise. Distinct canonical A-label hostnames also emit confusable_domain if the UTS #39 skeletons of the complete ToUnicode hostnames match. Compare at onboarding and after name, host or policy changes. Reindex atomically, index all holders of a collision symmetrically, and provide domain-first lookup. No enrollment or public outage is caused solely by a similar name. Never disclose pending or rejected applicants in peer links or flags. A name match indicates ambiguity, not brand ownership.
x-protocol-rules.identityConsent: Show the exact primary host and permanent ID at selection, confirmation and on all trust claims. Bind new consent to the verified partner, canonical domain, handoff authority and identityRevision, and recheck before dispatch. For a first selection with collision signals, or a changed domain since an existing pin, require that actor's matching current server-side pin or an independently supplied expected domain and observed revision. Do not copy this expected domain from a candidate row, referrer or badge parameter. A disagreement returns 409 (identity_confirmation_required, identity_mismatch or stale_identity) without issuing a handoff or new effect. Collision flags alone do not invalidate an otherwise current pin. Confirmed selection can establish a new actor-scoped pin after independent domain entry. Previously recorded receipts identify the binding used at the time.
x-protocol-rules.websiteBadge: Only active production capabilities with current verified domain bindings can generate a positive badge. Build the script-free embedded document on the dedicated cookieless Agent Commons host. Every ancestor must match the exact currently verified website HTTPS origin via the HTTP CSP frame-ancestors directive. Escape all displayed text as text. Badge clicks always open the permanent first-party profile. Never use a display name or a user-supplied URL to construct the destination. Send no-store on active and inactive public responses, purge retained CDN variants on change and disallow stale-on-error; an already open frame is a snapshot, and the destination rechecks status. The shared public template serves no personalized data and sets no cookies. Canonical open-in-new-tab links remain usable without the embed. Static placements and copied pixels carry no separate authority.
x-protocol-rules.authorization: Derive actor and organization from the session, partnerId from the confidential client, and environment from the serving origin. Enforce object assignment and current enrollment on every request. For a verifier role the same party must be an accepted custodian. Human mutations require same-origin and CSRF protection. Partner machine tokens cannot approve an application, create a user grant, publish tasks or trigger payout. Use TLS and Cache-Control: no-store for every private response.
x-protocol-rules.idempotency: Persist a key per logical mutation under environment, authenticated actor, operation and resource. For repeated identical requests return the recorded result after checking caller access. Reuse with a different payload or conflicting terminal effect returns 409. Keep replay records through reconciliation and at least the advertised retry window of seven days thereafter. Receipt IDs, terminal commands and reservation uniqueness remain durable across retry-cache expiry. Binding checks and writes must be atomic. The OAuth token endpoint uses one-use assertion jti and fresh assertions on retry.
x-protocol-rules.artifacts: Schemas use an ID plus the digest of exact immutable bytes. Execution requires task-scoped read access for each input and uploads for results; a supplied URL is never an authority. Limit JSON bodies to 64 KiB and artifact bytes to 8 MiB. Redact raw grants, JWS tokens and artifact content from ordinary logs.
x-protocol-rules.signatures: Verify compact JWS with a protected alg=Ed25519, registered kid and purpose-specific typ. Select keys from the local accepted registry only. Enforce exact issuer, audience, environment and payload binding; reject private key claims, unknown critical headers and remote key URLs. The partner API base URL without trailing slash is the receipt and handoff audience. Challenge audience is separately issued. Preserve historical verification material. Reject first-seen future-dated statements beyond 60 s; issue receipts promptly and preserve evidence of the actual operation when resolving older commands. For recovery receipts, establish the alternative signatory using the independently verified enrollment recovery channel, pin its thumbprint and identity to this case under dual control, and use protected typ partner-recovery+jwt scoped to the case. RFC 9864 defines fully specified Ed25519. JWT durations are checked with at most 60 s clock tolerance. Reject duplicate JSON member names and unknown protected headers.
x-protocol-rules.onboarding: Applicant cannot approve its own operational capabilities. Automated DNS proofs and comparison of public names run independently of that review. Sandbox key proof grants fixture-only scopes. Production review uses current domain evidence, a passing sandbox report and catalog coverage. Recheck identity, capability and profile at publication, consent and dispatch.
x-protocol-rules.operations: At-least-once delivery. Record commandId before executing. A definitive no-effect failure is terminal for that command. Unknown moves to uncertain and permits only lookup of that ID or reconciled terminal evidence. Refuse inconsistent terminal evidence and place it in operator review. Timeout cannot prove an external effect was absent. A reservation remains exclusively assigned until a confirmed terminal release or return. If a partner is suspended or revoked, revoke all online access immediately, preserve old evidence and reconcile legal outstanding obligations through the two-person recovery procedure.

post.summary: Start or renew proof for an exact website or handoff host
post.description: A fresh applicant administrator session can start the initial claim, stage a host or handoff URL replacement, or renew an existing proof. A partner token with domains:renew is confined to the already recorded host and URL of its own application; it cannot claim a new domain, move an enrollment, or unsuspend an application. Authorize the identity-maintenance scope for an expired lease only for that existing partner and host. A pending challenge reserves no public identity. The server polls DNS, binds challenge and expected application revision atomically and audits the outcome. Reuse of a token for another partner, host, purpose or environment fails.

201.description: Private challenge issued. The administrator or its DNS agent installs the TXT record before expiry.

get.summary: Read DNS challenge state after automatic verification
get.description: Only an authorized administrator or the same partner's scoped renewal worker can read the challenge. Polling does not extend its lifetime. A mismatched application returns 404.

200.description: Current challenge state derived by the site.

servers.description: Configured production API origin. Never serve sandbox, pending or unpublished applicants here.

get.description: Use the immutable partnerId. The same canonical record backs the profile page, badge and eligible catalog projection. Derive status from current capability acceptance and proof freshness on every read. Return retained, explicitly inactive identity after suspension, revocation or proof expiry. Never reveal private applications. Serve no redirects, identity-dependent cookies, permissive cache or applicant-chosen destinations.

404.description: Generic unavailable state for unpublished or unknown IDs, including sandbox and rejected applications. Same normal form for every private reason.

get.summary: Open an organization's canonical Agent Commons web page
get.description: Public verification destination for customers arriving from a badge. Render the same public profile as the JSON operation. Show the exact full verified website hostname, current or historical status, accepted capabilities and links to published similar identities. Profile navigation stays on the configured first-party HTTPS origin and the route is stable across display-name or key changes. Treat unknown and never-onboarded IDs alike.

200.description: Canonical public organization page with a current status or historical inactive notice.

Content-Security-Policy.description: The full trust page cannot be embedded.

404.description: Generic unavailable state for unpublished or unknown IDs, including sandbox and rejected applications. Same normal form for every private reason.

servers.description: Dedicated cookie-free production badge origin controlled by Agent Commons. Deploy with host-only login cookies on the main site.

get.description: After production activation the partner console offers the fixed iframe and plain-link fallback shown in x-partner-badge-examples. Construct both URLs at the configured HTTPS origins using the immutable partner ID and validated ASCII domain. Emit a linked badge only if the requested domain exactly matches the current verified website and the public status is active. Render a neutral unframeable response for a mismatched, expired or inactive binding; unknown IDs return the same neutral body with 404. No cookies, scripts, redirects, tracking pixels or referrer-based decisions. The passive link opens /partners/{partnerId} on the trusted first-party site in a new tab with noopener and noreferrer. Archived screenshots or copied markup establish no identity.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Exact verified primary A-label host for this embed. It cannot supply an origin, path, brand label or redirect URL.

200.description: Live badge or neutral unavailable response.

Content-Security-Policy.description: Set as an HTTP header on every response. For the active state, frame-ancestors contains only the assigned exact HTTPS website origin. Every ancestor must match. For any other state use frame-ancestors 'none'. Never emit wildcard, Referer, request host or query text as a source.

404.description: Generic unavailable state for unpublished or unknown IDs, including sandbox and rejected applications. Same normal form for every private reason.

post.summary: Apply for partner
post.description: Verified organization administrator. Register the requested catalog and public key. Derive owner and environment from authentication and deployment. A fresh application returns its challenge; a proof establishes key possession only.

get.description: Show applications owned by the acting organization. A separately authorized operator can inspect the review queue. Cursor is bound to environment, principal and filter.
Applicant organization admin or assigned platform reviewer. Cross-organization reads receive 404. Return the current key challenge if applicable.

post.summary: Change the name shown for an organization
post.description: An administrator of the applicant organization submits the current application revision. Recompute comparison signals for all affected published partners. A display-name edit preserves the permanent ID, exact domain and identity revision used by current grants.

post.summary: Manage partner key
post.description: Organization administrator with fresh authentication can register a locally generated candidate key, refresh its expired challenge, or revoke a key immediately. An independent incident operator can revoke compromised material. Each candidate must pass its own proof before activation. Reject stale expectedRevision; revoked keys cannot gain new authority.

post.summary: Prove partner key
post.description: Applicant organization administrator submits a compact JWS made by the candidate private key, bound to the issued nonce, application, deployment and key. Sandbox proof grants fixture-only access in sandbox_testing. A production application with matching passing sandbox report moves to in_review. Rotation requires active administrator authorization, valid proof, bounded overlap and an auditable old-key retirement.

post.summary: Start partner conformance
post.description: Sandbox only, after key proof. Platform issues fixture commands through the normal feed and tests supported capabilities. Bind report to organization, catalog digest, protocol version and suite revision; approval checks freshness and equality to the requested production catalog.

get.description: Read progress, sanitized failures and immutable final report. Application owners and reviewers only. Successful completion makes the sandbox application eligible for review.

post.summary: Review partner application
post.description: Independent platform trust operator with fresh authentication. Approve an eligible in_review application and supported subset, reject, suspend, resume after revalidation or permanently revoke. Applicants cannot approve their organization. A suspended partner receives no new assignments. Keep old evidence and use supervised reconciliation for outstanding effects. Approval checks both current DNS bindings. Publish the production profile only after first activation; suspension or revocation updates the public status and disables framing of the badge immediately.

post.summary: Start partner handoff
post.description: Actor must be authorized for this task: funder for reserve, claimant for run, eligible contributor for receive. Check accepted catalog and current version. Create a short-lived consent session, then open the exact registered partner page with a form POST. No credentials in URLs. Multiple winners require separately reserved inventory and beneficiary grants. Return the frozen website identity and exact separately verified handoff hostname before opening the partner login. Withhold handoff if proof, capability, identity revision or the expected domain check fails.

get.description: Only the initiating signed-in actor can poll this resource. Display task and grant ceilings and, after attestation, the masked account label before confirmation. Return 404 to other actors.

post.summary: Exchange partner handoff
post.description: Only the addressed partner can exchange the browser-delivered one-use code before expiry. It receives just the task-scoped offer. Present the exact grant and obtain authenticated account-holder approval before attesting.

post.summary: Attest partner handoff
post.description: Verify typ partner-handoff+jwt against HandoffClaims, designated issuer, key, environment, audience, nonce, actor, grant, task and expiry. Attach verified account label for the initiating actor to confirm. Do not assign work or reserve from this step alone.

post.summary: Decide partner handoff
post.description: The initiating signed-in actor confirms a live attested handoff or declines it. Recheck task eligibility, account and terms version. After confirmation only the intended partner receives grantRef on the corresponding command. Revoked or expired task grants cannot be dispatched. A subsequent charge requires fresh consent. A confirmed grant can be withdrawn by its initiating actor until first consumption. Serialize withdrawal against command creation; the losing operation re-reads state. After consumption return 409 and reconcile the original effect. Recheck the stored ID, identityRevision, both verified hosts and current status before confirmation and dispatch. A changed binding produces stale_identity. Consent from the old binding cannot authorize a fresh effect.

get.description: Pull this partner’s assigned outstanding commands in stable creation order, within the token environment and accepted catalog. The cursor is an opaque page position. Restart at the first page to rediscover still-open work. The partner persists commandId before starting any effect; repeated delivery never authorizes another charge. Uncertain commands may be reconciled only.

Look up an assigned command by durable ID after a timeout, cursor expiry or restart. Check authoritative state before work. A successful or failed terminal command is read-only. An uncertain command requires lookup of the original execution at the partner; recover signed evidence for that same effect.

post.summary: Post partner receipt
post.description: Submit a compact Ed25519 JWS with decoded ReceiptClaims. Check assignment, environment, audience, key, time and replay before accepting kind-specific bindings. Identical signed evidence returns its stored acknowledgement even after terminal settlement. Different terminal outcomes conflict. A failed outcome certifies absence of effect; an unknown outcome leaves settlement pending. Persist receipt, state transition and downstream outbox atomically.

post.summary: Upload partner artifact
post.description: Only the assigned model-provider may upload bytes for a run within its input/output policy. Upload before signing the outcome. Server computes SHA-256 over raw bytes, verifies the supplied digest and returns a command-bound handle. Unreferenced uploads expire. Eight MiB per artifact in this profile; reject unapproved media types.

parameters.name: Content-Digest
parameters.description: RFC 9530 field for the exact body.

parameters.name: X-Artifact-Media-Type
parameters.description: Declared logical media type, checked against the command policy.

get.description: Return only input bytes specifically referenced by a command assigned to this partner. Confirm the digest against the command before use. Binding an output from one command to a subsequent verification command is a site-authorized operation. Eight MiB per artifact.

200.description: Immutable artifact bytes, transmitted as octet stream.

Content-Digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the exact returned bytes.

get.description: Project actors discover eligible provider, holder and verification capabilities. Filter by capability and paginate; responses are projections, so publication and assignment recheck eligibility against the pinned profile. Provide either domainAscii for exact eligible-primary-host lookup or name for display-name comparison. If both are present return 400. A domain read plus any capability filter returns at most one current production partner; an empty result never falls back to a name match. A name search includes exact, normalized, confusable and near candidates, ordered by stable canonical domain and ID with no implicit selection. Bind cursor to actor, environment and all filters.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: Exact immutable ID. Supply only one of partnerId, domainAscii or name.

parameters.name: domainAscii
parameters.description: Exact canonical website host. Mutually exclusive with name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Compare the supplied display name using the enrolled name-comparison policy. Mutually exclusive with domainAscii.

get.description: Append-only, application-scoped history ordered by revision and event ID. Owners and independent reviewers may see sanitized events and visible decision reasons. Restrict private incident evidence to the operator vault.

Trusted incident or settlement operator. List open holds, uncertain effects and in-progress settlements ordered by age; filter by task or partner. Include suspended and revoked partners. Expose no account numbers, prompts or credentials.

post.summary: Reconcile partner obligation
post.description: Incident operator with fresh authentication opens a case against an existing command and freezes normal dispatch for this obligation. A different settlement operator authorizes lookup or transmission of the SAME already-eligible release/return through the holder’s independently authenticated recovery channel. Recheck winner, terms, grant and unspent hold at authorization. Consult the holder ledger before transmission and require its durable commandId deduplication, including across online and offline channels. This route cannot authorize a new run. Archive the signed external statement and channel verification under the supplied sourceReference. The evidence submitter and confirmer must differ. After validating the separately obtained recovery signer, exact original bindings, legal state transition and vault digest, apply the ordinary terminal transition and downstream outbox atomically. Missing or conflicting evidence leaves the obligation open. Block revoked online keys and expired tokens even in recovery.

get.description: Incident and settlement operators can inspect the canonical case and pending action by ID after an ambiguous write.

post.summary: Exchange a signed client assertion for a scoped partner token
post.description: Authenticate using the client assertion in the form body. On an ambiguous network response send a fresh signed assertion with a new jti; this operation issues credentials and never authorizes an external effect.

200.description: Short-lived token authorized for this environment, admission and granted scopes.

400.description: Invalid grant request, client assertion or scope.

Session.name: uw_session
Session.description: Verified human session. Request authorization depends on acting organization, task rights and independent platform operator role. Browser writes require the deployment CSRF controls.

PartnerOAuth.description: OAuth client_credentials with private_key_jwt (RFC 7523). POST form grant_type=client_credentials, client_id=partnerId, scope, client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer and client_assertion. Sign using registered kid/Ed25519 with typ partner-client-auth+jwt and iss=sub=partnerId, aud=absolute token URL, jti, iat, exp at most five minutes later. Reject reused assertions. Success follows OAuth token response semantics (access_token, token_type=Bearer, expires_in <= 300, granted scope); no refresh token. Validate the environment, issuer, audience and enrollment on every resource request. Tokens are server side only.

scopes.artifacts:read: Read artifacts bound to assigned commands.
scopes.artifacts:write: Upload output bytes for an assigned model run.
scopes.handoffs:write: Exchange one-time codes and attest user-approved scoped grants.
scopes.domains:renew: Renew proof for the existing website or handoff host of this application only.

HumanBearer.description: First-party user session transported as a Bearer token for permitted machine/MCP access. Resolve the same acting tenant, user, object authorization, fresh-auth and operator constraints as the browser session. A partner service token is a different issuer/audience and cannot substitute.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-generated high-entropy identity for one logical write. Reuse on timeout for identical intent.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor, scoped to principal and filters. Omit to start.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, expired, revoked or invalid authentication.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated principal lacks operation scope or role.

NotFound.description: Resource not visible to this principal or absent.

Conflict.description: Conflicting idempotency payload, stale revision, conflicting outcome or impossible transition. Re-read current state.

Gone.description: One-time grant, challenge or command-start deadline has lapsed.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: Media type outside the allowed profile.

InvalidEvidence.description: Authentic request has invalid schema, evidence or task/asset/rule binding.

RateLimited.description: Rate or concurrency limit reached. Retry with jitter after the indicated delay.

Unavailable.description: Temporarily unavailable. Retry reconciliation with the original operation identity.

acceptance.description: Required to publish a rewarded task. Optional on volunteer work.

provenance.description: Require a receipt from the approved provider for this model and usage limit.

reward.description: The holder must reserve the entire asset before publication. Specify a deadline earlier than holdUntil.

demo.description: Recorded issuer is a local demonstration partner.

DomainAscii.description: Exact fully qualified lowercase DNS host in ASCII (A-label) representation, without a trailing dot. Apply Unicode 17 UTS #46 nontransitional ToASCII with STD3, Bidi, ContextJ and DNS-length checks. Registry validation also excludes public suffixes, IP literals, nonpublic hosts and wildcard names. The public suffix list includes private rules.

DomainChallengeRequest.description: Use the URL registered on the application. A freshly authenticated organization administrator can stage a new exact HTTPS URL using replacementUrl. Validate its host and default HTTPS port, reject credentials, queries, fragments and unapproved redirects. DNS proof covers only the named host. Renewal-only tokens must omit replacementUrl and may address only their existing bound host.

DomainChallenge.description: Private DNS TXT challenge. Its high-entropy value binds this challenge to the application, revision, environment, purpose and exact host. Poll this resource for the site's DNS result. A consumed value cannot start another lease.

PartnerIdentity.description: Public identity fields shared by the profile, selector and consent view. domainAscii is the last proved website host, interpreted with enrollment status and proof times. identityRevision changes for a different bound domain, transfer or handoff authority. Routine key rotation, fresh proof of the same host and peer collisions alone preserve it. relatedPartners lists up to 32 active, already public peer IDs in stable order; collisionSignals summarizes the whole comparison even if the list is truncated. Never disclose pending enrollment metadata.

profilePath.description: Deployment-owned canonical profile path using the complete immutable partnerId, resolved only against the configured first-party web origin.

ExpectedPartnerIdentity.description: Supply an independently known hostname and the selected profile's observed identity revision. The site compares against the selected immutable ID and current verified binding. The UI must never auto-fill the hostname from an ambiguous result. A server-side pin for this actor and current binding can supply this check.

PublicPartnerProfile.description: Anonymous projection of a previously activated production partner. asOf is the calculation time. Negative states retain the last proved identity with a warning; only active current evidence may show capabilities as accepted. Raw proofs, private contacts, keys, handoff URLs, tasks and financial data are excluded.

demo.description: This fictional organization belongs to the local review fixture.

Digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes. For terms and rule manifests, hash the immutable bytes archived by Agent Commons for that version.

Asset.description: An immutable, issuer-qualified catalog ID and unit distinguish vouchers, currency subunits, compute credits or other transferable inventory. Reject cash equivalents, partial quantities or mismatched units.

quantity.description: Positive integer count of the catalogued asset’s smallest deliverable unit. Use a string to preserve exact quantities.

Artifact.description: Immutable bytes; dereference only at the artifact endpoint for the assigned command.

Rule.description: Accepted verifier catalog entry with immutable executable identity.

PublicKey.description: Base64url public bytes. Reject reused kid for different material, private fields and keys known to a different environment.

ModelOffer.description: The provider can attest the served model. List only reasoning efforts that it can substantiate for that model. An empty list supports model-only tasks.

Catalog.description: Empty lists declare no support. Bind exact offered versions on approval. The verifier capability is available only to accepted custodians; check eligibility on every assignment.

ApplicationRequest.description: The authenticated organization is the applicant. Agent Commons normalizes the website and handoff hosts and verifies exact control through DNS challenges. Production additionally requires a passing sandbox report, distinct key material and approval for the requested capabilities. The operator independently verifies the recovery contact channel. Display names and registration order grant no exclusive name rights.

KeyChallenge.description: One-use random 256-bit nonce. Sign the exact ChallengeClaims within five minutes.

ChallengeClaims.description: Compact JWS with Ed25519, candidate kid and typ partner-key-proof+jwt. iss is the assigned partnerId, aud the challenge audience. Signing and expiry times are Unix seconds.

thumbprint.description: Base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the public key, RFC 7638.

Application.description: Organization administrators and independent reviewers see the current application. challenge is present while proof is pending. Approved capabilities must be a subset of the request. Enrollment detail only. Contact details and key diagnostics are private. Suspension and revocation invalidate all online tokens for the application immediately; review a new approval before admitting a different capability set. domainChallengeIds identifies the most recent website and handoff challenges for authorized polling. A pending domain replacement never overwrites the verified binding.

demo.description: Server-assigned marker for a fictional review organization.

viewer.description: Private abilities derived from the current viewer and the application owner.

taskActivity.description: Recent assigned operations, newest first. Available to the managing organization on the local demo production application detail.

recoveryRole.description: The signed-in operator’s assigned recovery role.

canReview.description: Current viewer can review applications as a site operator.

canManage.description: Current viewer can manage applications in the acting tenant.

badgeOrigin.description: Configured dedicated HTTPS host for website badges.

ConformanceRun.description: The site derives results from sandbox commands, receipts and negative vectors. Applicants can start or repeat tests; they cannot supply the verdict.

Problem.description: Stable reason examples include stale_revision, idempotency_conflict, binding_mismatch, transition_conflict and insufficient_scope. Do not expose foreign resource identities.

HandoffRequest.description: Use the signed-in initiating actor, never a caller-supplied account identity. The server derives immutable charge limits or asset and actorRef from the task and its claim. If this actor lacks a current pin for an ambiguous partner, or its previous binding changed, require the independently supplied expected domain and observed revision. Match the full selected partnerId, verified domain, revision and current capabilities atomically. Omission in these cases returns identity_confirmation_required.

HandoffStart.description: The browser form POSTs handoffId and startCode to this exact registered URL. Single-use code bound to actor, partner, environment, task and terms. Site polls the authenticated status endpoint in the originating tab.

demo.description: The grant is issued by a local demonstration partner.

RunGrantTerms.description: The provider enforces both token ceilings and authorizes at most one billable run. Omit effort for a model-only grant. When supplied, effort is an approved value for this model and must match the dispatched action.

ReserveGrantTerms.description: Authority to reserve this asset once for this task until at least holdUntil.

HandoffOffer.description: actorRef is pairwise for this partner and actor. Partner signs the approved terms only after the account holder explicitly selects the source and approves them on the partner site.

HandoffClaims.description: typ partner-handoff+jwt. iss is partnerId. aud is the deployment partner API audience. grantRef is a single-use, partner-internal reference, not a bearer credential. accountLabel is a masked human-readable source.

demo.description: The grant is issued by a local demonstration partner.

HandoffDecision.description: Only the initiating actor can confirm. Require the latest task terms and a live matching attestation; declines can close any pre-confirmation state. Withdraw a confirmed, unconsumed grant atomically against dispatch. A consumed grant cannot cancel or reverse an external effect.

ReceiveGrantTerms.description: Authority to deliver this exact asset to the contributor-selected destination at this custodian for this task.

RunAction.description: model and any requested effort must match the approved task terms, catalog and confirmed grant. Omitted effort leaves that setting to the provider.

VerifyAction.description: The rule and referenced fixtures pin the inputs for an executable check. The platform can also execute its own accepted rules internally.

ReleaseAction.description: grantRef is the confirmed receive handoff for the winning contributor at this holder, bound to task, terms and exact asset.

ReturnAction.description: Return only to the original funding source; the reservation identifies that source at its issuer.

ReserveOutcome.description: Confirms exclusive control of the complete reserved units. holdUntil is the earliest guaranteed holding deadline. The holder must retain control through unresolved settlement and accept only one release or return.

RunOutcome.description: Attest the actual model and exact input and output bytes. Include actualEffort only when the provider can substantiate it. Model-only provenance requires actualModel to match the requested model. If the task also specifies effort, the receipt must attest that value to satisfy provenance. Record truthful mismatches and missing effort as delivered evidence, withhold the required provenance badge and reward until the requirement is met, and never infer a served value from the request.

VerifyOutcome.description: A failed predicate is a completed verification with a rejected verdict; technical inability to decide is an operational outcome.

FailedOutcome.description: Definitive evidence this command had no external effect. A charged model run or uncertain transfer cannot report this outcome.

UnknownOutcome.description: Effect may have occurred. Look up the original provider operation by commandId and reconcile. Never execute again on this evidence alone.

Command.description: Immutable action and task binding. deadline is the last time to START a new effect. Late evidence about a prior effect remains admissible for reconciliation; retrieve current state before acting.

CommandPage.description: Read-only at-least-once delivery; listing does not claim, acknowledge or drop a command.

ReceiptClaims.description: Decoded signed receipt. Compact JWT with protected alg Ed25519, kid and typ partner-receipt+jwt, fixed issuer and per-environment audience. The site checks all bindings against the stored command, catalog, grant, identity and actual artifact bytes. Deduplicate the signed statement by issuer and jti and the effect by commandId.

PartnerProfile.description: Only capabilities and catalog entries currently approved for this caller and environment. Exclude internal contact details, key material, pending applications and personal account data. Production eligibility requires a current verified binding. Display the complete primary host and link to the full immutable ID from identity. Sandbox projections use the sandbox origin, carry a Sandbox label, and confer no public listing.

demo.description: This selectable partner is a fictional local review organization.

trustedForActor.description: True when the authenticated viewer already pinned this exact current identity.

webOrigin.description: Canonical origin of public organization pages when configured.

Obligation.description: Internal operator view. A succeeded reserve remains visible as held until exclusive confirmed settlement. An uncertain execution remains visible until resolved.

oneOf.description: Use a compact JWS with decoded RecoveryClaims from the independently verified recovery signatory; archive the signed bytes in the restricted case vault. evidenceDigest is SHA-256 of the exact compact JWS ASCII bytes. sourceReference identifies the source record obtained through the verified channel.

availableActions.description: Actions this operator may take at the current case revision.

ClientAssertionClaims.description: iss=sub=partnerId, aud=exact absolute token endpoint, exp within five minutes of iat, one-use jti, protected typ partner-client-auth+jwt.

RecoveryClaims.description: Decoded partner-recovery+jwt signed by the separately verified case signatory. aud is the absolute case resource URL. Check recoveryId, issuer, command and all ReceiptClaims bindings. The operator’s submit_evidence request supplies the vault sourceReference and digest of the compact JWS bytes; verify those against the archived statement before confirmation.

externalDocs.description: Task coordination design and example publication/settlement terms.
